steps.title: Import Vue composition API functions (ref, onMounted) and axios
steps.instruction: Import ref and onMounted from 'vue', and import axios from 'axios'
steps.hint: Use import statements at the top of your file to bring in the necessary dependencies.
steps.seedCode: // Import ref and onMounted from 'vue', and import axios from 'axios'
steps.expectedOutcome: The required dependencies for the composable are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: ref and onMounted are imported from 'vue', and axios is imported from 'axios'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Vue composition API functions and axios, which are essential for building the useFetch composable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported all three items: ref and onMounted from 'vue', and axios from 'axios'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import ref and onMounted from 'vue', and axios from 'axios'.

steps.title: Create the generic useFetch composable function
steps.instruction: Define a function called useFetch that takes a url parameter and returns an object. The function should be a composable that can be used in Vue components.
steps.hint: Start by writing a function declaration or arrow function with the name useFetch and a url parameter.
steps.seedCode:
// Import ref and onMounted from 'vue', and import axios from 'axios'

// Define the useFetch function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A useFetch function is defined with a url parameter, ready to be implemented as a composable.
successCriteria: The useFetch function is defined with a url parameter and returns an object (even if empty for now).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the useFetch function structure. This will serve as the foundation for our generic data fetching composable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a function named useFetch that takes a url parameter and returns an object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function definition doesn't match what's needed. Create a function called useFetch with a url parameter that returns an object.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state variables for data, loading, and error
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, create three ref variables: data (initialized as null), loading (initialized as false), and error (initialized as null).
steps.hint: Use the ref function from Vue to create reactive variables. Remember to import ref if you haven't already.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function will have three reactive state variables ready to track API data, loading status, and errors.
successCriteria: Three ref variables are created inside useFetch: data (null), loading (false), and error (null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the reactive state variables needed for tracking API responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some ref variables, but make sure you have all three: data, loading, and error with their correct initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFetch function doesn't contain the required three ref variables. Check that you've created data, loading, and error with ref().

steps.title: Define the fetchData async function inside useFetch
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, define an async function named fetchData that will handle the HTTP request.
steps.hint: Create an async function that will later contain the axios call and state updates.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function now contains an empty async fetchData function ready to be implemented.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchData is defined inside the useFetch function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the fetchData function. Next we'll implement its logic.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined an async function named fetchData inside useFetch.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchData async function isn't properly defined inside useFetch. Check the syntax.

steps.title: Call fetchData when the component mounts using onMounted
steps.instruction: Inside the useFetch function, call the onMounted lifecycle hook and pass it fetchData so that data fetching happens automatically when a component using useFetch is mounted.
steps.hint: Remember that onMounted is a function that takes a callback. You can call it directly inside useFetch and pass fetchData as the callback.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function now automatically triggers data fetching when a component using it is mounted.
successCriteria: onMounted is called inside useFetch with fetchData as its argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the onMounted lifecycle hook to automatically fetch data when the component mounts.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling onMounted with fetchData as the callback inside the useFetch function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The onMounted lifecycle hook isn't properly set up to call fetchData. Remember to call onMounted inside useFetch and pass fetchData to it.

steps.title: Return the reactive state and fetchData function from useFetch
steps.instruction: At the end of the useFetch function, return an object containing the three reactive state variables (data, loading, error) and the fetchData function.
steps.hint: Make sure to return an object with properties that expose the state and the function so the component can use them.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useFetch function now returns an object containing the reactive state and the fetchData method, making them available to any component that calls useFetch.
successCriteria: The useFetch function returns an object with properties data, loading, error, and fetchData.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully returned the state and method from the composable, allowing components to access the fetched data, loading status, error, and the ability to refetch.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning an object with all four properties: data, loading, error, and fetchData.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useFetch function needs to return an object containing the reactive state variables and the fetchData function so the component can use them.

steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'UserList' with a script setup section and a template that returns a single div element.
steps.hint: Use the Vue single-file component structure with <script setup> and <template> tags. The template should contain a single div element.

steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a Vue component named 'UserList' with the basic structure ready to use the useFetch composable.
successCriteria: The component is named 'UserList' and contains both <script setup> and <template> sections with a single div element in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the UserList component with the proper Vue structure. This gives us a foundation to use our useFetch composable.

steps.title: Use the useFetch composable in the component with a sample API URL
steps.instruction: Inside the component's script setup, call useFetch with the URL 'https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts/1' and destructure data, loading, and error from the returned object.
steps.hint: Call the useFetch function you created earlier, passing the sample URL as an argument. Use destructuring assignment to extract the three reactive state variables.

steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has access to the reactive data, loading, and error states from the useFetch composable, ready to display API data.
successCriteria: useFetch is called with the sample URL, and data, loading, and error are destructured from its return value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully called the useFetch composable and extracted the reactive state variables.

successCriteria: A paragraph element with v-if="loading" and text 'Loading...' is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the loading state.

steps.instruction: In your template, add conditional rendering to display the fetched data when it's available, or show an error message if an error occurred.
steps.hint: Use Vue's template syntax with v-if or v-else to conditionally render different content based on the loading, error, and data states.

steps.expectedOutcome: The template will now show the fetched data when available, display an error message if there's an error, and show loading state while fetching.
